text: But Mrs. Penniman’s imagination was restless, and the evening paper failed on this occasion to enchain it. “If you succumb to the dread of your father’s wrath,” she said, “I don’t know what will become of us.” “Did he tell you to say these things to me?” “He told me to use my influence.” “You must be mistaken,” said Catherine. “He trusts me.” “I hope he may never repent of it!” And Mrs. Penniman gave a little sharp slap to her newspaper. She knew not what to make of her niece, who had suddenly become stern and contradictious. This tendency on Catherine’s part was presently even more apparent.
